learning_outcomes.text: Classify materials and explain their fundamental structures.
Analyze the effects of atomic structure and interatomic bonds on material properties.
Identify crystal structures and crystal defects.
Explain the mechanical, thermal, electrical, and magnetic properties of materials.
Interpret diffusion and phase diagrams to analyze material transformations.
Discuss the structural and physical properties of polymers, ceramics, and composite materials.
Explain how heat treatments affect the properties of metal alloys.
Use material selection criteria to choose the most suitable materials for engineering problems.
Analyze material failures (fatigue, corrosion, fracture) and propose preventive methods.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to materials science, classification of materials
Mechanical properties of materials (hardness, ductility, strength, etc.)
Electrical and magnetic properties of materials
Material selection criteria and engineering applications
Material failures: fatigue, corrosion, and fracture
assessment_rules: The final success grade is determined by the contribution of in-term activities and the final exam grade. The Midterm Examination contributes 40% to the final grade. The Final Examination contributes 60% to the final grade.
bibliography: Callister, W. D., & Rethwisch, D. G. (2020). Materials Science and Engineering: An Introduction. Wiley.
Smith, W. F., & Hashemi, J. (2019). Foundations of Materials Science and Engineering. McGraw-Hill Education.
Shackelford, J. F. (2015). Introduction to Materials Science for Engineers. Pearson.
